content.title: About
content.content: Chewing gum is a sweet or flavored rubbery mass designed for chewing. It typically consists of a gum base, sweeteners, flavorings, and sometimes softening agents. Chewing gum is not intended to be swallowed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first modern chewing gum was invented by William S. White in 1869.
In the 1970s, chewing gum was used in space missions to help astronauts relieve stress.
Sugar‑free gum contains sweetener substitutes such as xylitol, which is beneficial for teeth.
Chewing gum can improve concentration and memory by increasing blood flow to the brain.
In some countries chewing gum is banned in schools due to the risk of it being swallowed.

items.title: Stimulates saliva production
items.content: Chewing increases saliva flow, which helps neutralize acids and reduces the risk of cavities.

items.title: Improves focus
items.content: Studies show that chewing can boost attention and short‑term memory.

items.title: Reduces stress
items.content: The mechanical act of chewing promotes relaxation and lowers cortisol levels.

items.title: Supports oral hygiene
items.content: Sugar‑free varieties with xylitol can inhibit the growth of cavity‑causing bacteria.

items.title: Aids smoking cessation
items.content: Chewing gum is often used as a nicotine replacement to curb cravings.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to flavorings, sweeteners, or the gum base.

items.title: Gastrointestinal discomfort
items.content: Excessive chewing can cause stomach upset, gas, or heartburn.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small pieces of gum can be dangerous for young children if swallowed.

items.title: Sweetener concerns
items.content: Sugar‑containing gum can promote cavities, while some sugar substitutes (e.g., sorbitol) may cause diarrhea in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chew the gum slowly without swallowing. Sugar‑free versions are recommended after meals to improve oral hygiene. Avoid chewing for more than 15‑20 minutes at a time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store gum in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package to prevent drying out and loss of flavor. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator.
